title: The lotus leaf
hookLine: a lotus leaf sits in the pond all day, and the water rolls off it in beads
carry: act fully, cling to nothing, like the lotus leaf

lines: STAY IN THE POND, NOT WET.
cards: Rain falls on a pond. The water gathers on a lotus leaf in bright beads, rolls to the edge, and slides off. The leaf has been in the water all its life.
It isn't wet. In the Bhagavad Gita, Arjuna wants to put down his bow and walk away from the battle. Krishna doesn't tell him to leave the pond.
In the fifth chapter he gives him that leaf, a picture of someone who acts fully in the world and isn't stained by it. This year the path read it on three tracks: karma, bhakti and jnana.

teach.h: NOT TOUCHED, LIKE A LOTUS LEAF.
teach.b: Here is the Gita's line, in paraphrase: one who acts while placing every action in Brahman, letting go of clinging, is not touched by wrong, as a lotus leaf is not touched by water.
Hold that leaf up to each of the year's three tracks. The karma track read Gita chapters three, four and five, and designed a year of service.
There the leaf means doing the work well and setting down the result.
The bhakti track read the Gita Govinda and the Bhagavata's tenth book, and sang kirtan. There the leaf turns into an offering.
Elsewhere the Gita has Krishna say, in paraphrase: whatever you do, whatever you eat, whatever you give, do it as an offering to me. The act is the same. Now it is a gift.
The jnana track read Shankara's Crest-Jewel of Discrimination and the Ashtavakra Gita. There the leaf is the witness.
Ashtavakra tells King Janaka, in paraphrase: you are not earth, water, fire, air or space; know yourself as the witness of all these. Three tracks, three readings of one leaf.
And the Gita itself, in the same chapter, says that only the childish call the path of knowledge and the path of action different; the one who truly stands in either reaches the fruit of both.
Read that way, the tracks aren't a contest. They're three ways up, and under all three sits one teaching: freedom doesn't mean leaving the world.

teach.h: STAY IN THE WATER. LET GO OF CLINGING.
teach.b: Stay in the water, do your dharma fully, and let go of clinging.

how: The paths of karma, bhakti and jnana are walked side by side and in combination: selfless work and service, devotion in worship and kirtan, and study and inquiry with a teacher; the Gita is read as holding all three.

o: a lotus flower offered at a shrine
a seat folded into the shape of a lotus
the lotus leaf, in water yet never wet

games.q: one leaf, three tracks — tap the pairs.
p: do the work, set down the result
in the water, not touched by it

s: the Gita says the lotus leaf stays dry because it stays out of the pond
the leaf lives in the water and still isn't touched by it: acting in the world, unstained.
in the Gita's fifth chapter, knowledge and action are called one by the wise
it says only the childish speak of them as different.
Ashtavakra tells Janaka he is made of earth, water and fire
he tells him he is none of these, but the witness of them all.

games.q: you've finished a piece of work and done it well. the result is out of your hands. what does the Gita's lotus leaf picture suggest?
o: hold on tight until the result comes in.
act fully, then let the result roll off, like water on a leaf.
next time, don't act at all.
games.why: the Gita pictures someone who acts, places the action in Brahman and lets go of clinging, untouched as a lotus leaf by water. it never says to stop acting.

practice: Bring to mind one ordinary task from today, a dish, an email, a drive, and hold it for a few breaths the karma way: done well, the result let go. Then the bhakti way: if you pray, see it as something offered.
Then the jnana way: notice the one who watches it being done, still and dry like the leaf, and don't pick a favorite.

wordCard.voice: Padma-patra. The lotus leaf, sitting in water all its life and never wet, the Gita's picture for the three tracks of karma, bhakti and jnana.

orig.note: Sanskrit, in Devanagari: padma-patra, lotus leaf, the Gita's picture in chapter five.

carryVoice: Your line: act fully, cling to nothing, like the lotus leaf. Krishna didn't send Arjuna out of the pond. Tomorrow, a boy and a mantra. See you tomorrow.
